HSALES-CTX-G1.title: Brightloom Relay product and pricing sheet
HSALES-CTX-G1.text:
Brightloom Relay - Product and Pricing Sheet (FY2026, rep-facing)
Kestrel Forge Software, Inc. | Effective 1 March 2026 | Owner: Revenue Operations

WHAT IT IS
Brightloom Relay is field-service scheduling and dispatch software for trades businesses with 5 to 500 field technicians (HVAC, plumbing, electrical, pest control, appliance repair). It replaces whiteboards, shared calendars and phone tag between the office and the field.

CORE MODULES
- Dispatch Board: a drag-and-drop dispatch board with every technician as a row and every job as a colour-coded block by status (Unassigned, Scheduled, En Route, On Site, Done). Dispatchers see live technician location, updated every 60 seconds while a tech is clocked in, plus skill tags and overtime warnings before they assign a job.
- Relay Field app (iOS and Android): job details, customer history, photos, checklists, signature capture and on-site quoting. The app works offline; jobs, notes and photos queue on the phone and sync when signal returns. Offline mode keeps up to 7 days of assigned jobs on the device.
- Customer notifications: automatic "on my way" text with a live arrival window. Each account includes 1,000 SMS messages per month; extra messages are $0.02 each.
- Route optimization: re-sequences a technician's day to cut drive time. Growth and Enterprise only.
- Invoicing and payments: invoice straight from the job, card-on-file, and sync to QuickBooks Online on all plans. NetSuite connector (Enterprise only).
- Reporting: first-time-fix rate, jobs per tech per day, revenue per job, on-time arrival percentage.

INTEGRATIONS
Native: QuickBooks Online, NetSuite (Enterprise only), Salesforce, HubSpot, Google Calendar, Microsoft 365 Calendar.
Not currently supported: SAP (any edition), Sage Intacct, Xero. Customers on these systems can use the open REST API (limit 600 requests per minute per account) or a nightly scheduled CSV export. There is no committed date for new accounting connectors; do not promise one.

PLANS AND LIST PRICING (per field technician seat)
- Starter: $29 per technician per month billed annually, or $34 billed monthly. Up to 15 technicians. Dispatch Board, Field app, notifications, QuickBooks Online sync. No route optimization.
- Growth: $54 per technician per month, billed annually only. 10-seat minimum. Everything in Starter plus route optimization, custom checklists, and Salesforce and HubSpot sync.
- Enterprise: custom pricing, minimum annual contract value $40,000. Everything in Growth plus the NetSuite connector, a sandbox environment, data residency choice and a named Customer Success Manager.
Office seats (dispatchers, office admins) are free up to 5 per account; each additional office seat is $15 per month.

ONE-TIME IMPLEMENTATION FEE
- Starter: self-serve onboarding, no fee.
- Growth: guided implementation, $2,500 one-time. Covers data import, 2 remote training sessions and 30 days of go-live support.
- Enterprise: scoped per project, starting at $7,500.

DISCOUNTING GUIDELINES (internal - do not read out)
- Multi-year prepay: 2-year term 8% off list, 3-year term 12% off list (Growth and Enterprise).
- Reps may approve up to 10% additional discount on their own. Above 10% needs Sales Director approval; above 20% needs CRO approval.
- Implementation fee waivers need Sales Director approval.
- Nonprofit pricing: 15% off Starter or Growth with documentation.
- No free trials. A 30-day paid pilot on Growth is available for up to 10 technicians at $64 per technician for the pilot month, credited against year one if the customer signs within 45 days of pilot end.

POSITIONING NOTES
Lead with dispatcher time saved and on-time arrivals, not features. Typical reference customers are 20 to 80 technician shops moving off a whiteboard or a shared calendar. Do not quote customer results by name without a signed reference agreement.

HSALES-CTX-C1.title: Brightloom Relay rep quick reference (merged draft)
HSALES-CTX-C1.text:
Brightloom Relay - Rep Quick Reference (DRAFT - merged from Q3 2025 and Q1 2026 versions)
Please check with RevOps before quoting anything from this page.

PLANS AT A GLANCE
- Starter: $29 per tech per month (annual). Up to 15 techs.
- Growth: $54 per tech per month (annual). Includes route optimization, custom checklists, CRM sync and single sign-on (SSO) with Okta or Google.
- Enterprise: custom, from $40,000 per year. Adds NetSuite, sandbox, data residency, named CSM.

CURRENT PROMO
Growth at $49 per tech per month for new logos who sign before quarter end. (Promo code GROW49.)

IMPLEMENTATION
Growth guided implementation is a flat $1,500. Enterprise is scoped.

INTEGRATIONS
QuickBooks Online, Xero, Salesforce, HubSpot, Google and Microsoft calendars. NetSuite on Enterprise.

SECURITY FAQ (copy-paste for prospects)
Q: Do you support SSO?
A: Yes. SAML SSO is available on the Enterprise plan.
Q: Are you SOC 2?
A: Yes, SOC 2 Type II. Report available under NDA.
Q: What is your uptime guarantee?
A: 99.95% on all paid plans, backed by service credits.

SUPPORT FAQ
Q: What uptime do you commit to contractually?
A: Enterprise customers get a 99.9% SLA. Starter and Growth have no contractual SLA; see the status page.
Q: Which accounting tools do you sync with?
A: QuickBooks Online on all plans, NetSuite on Enterprise. Xero is not currently supported.

DEMO TIPS
Show the Dispatch Board first, then a technician's day in the Field app, then the invoice. Keep the demo under 25 minutes and leave time for questions.

OBJECTION NOTES
If a prospect says they were told SSO is included on Growth, confirm the plan and escalate to your manager before agreeing to anything.

HSALES-CTX-G2.title: Brightloom Relay security, support and terms summary
HSALES-CTX-G2.text:
Brightloom Relay - Security, Support and Commercial Terms Summary
Kestrel Forge Software, Inc. | Version 2026.2 | Owner: Legal and Security

SECURITY AND COMPLIANCE
- SOC 2 Type II: the current report covers 1 January to 31 December 2025. It is shared under a mutual NDA through the customer trust portal, usually within 2 business days of the NDA being signed.
- ISO 27001: not certified. Kestrel Forge has not committed to a certification date; do not state one.
- Penetration testing: annual test by an independent firm. An executive summary letter is available under NDA; the full report is not shared.
- Encryption: AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2 or higher in transit.
- Hosting: AWS. Default region is US (Ohio). EU data residency (Frankfurt) is available on Enterprise only.
- Single sign-on: SAML 2.0 SSO (Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace) is Enterprise only, as is SCIM user provisioning. Starter and Growth use email and password with optional authenticator-app two-factor.
- Health data: Brightloom Relay is not designed to store protected health information, and Kestrel Forge does not sign Business Associate Agreements.
- Subprocessors are listed on the trust portal; customers get 30 days notice of changes.

SUPPORT
- Starter: email and in-app chat, 8am to 6pm US Central, Monday to Friday. Target first response: 1 business day.
- Growth: adds phone support in the same hours. Priority 1 (system down) first response within 4 business hours.
- Enterprise: 24/7 phone line for Priority 1, first response within 1 hour, plus a named Customer Success Manager.

UPTIME
- Enterprise SLA: 99.9% monthly uptime for the Dispatch Board and the API. Service credits: 10% of the monthly fee if uptime falls below 99.9%, 25% if it falls below 99.0%. Credits are the sole remedy and must be requested within 30 days of the end of the affected month. The mobile app's offline mode is not covered by the SLA.
- Starter and Growth: no contractual SLA. A public status page shows live and historical uptime.

CONTRACT TERMS
- Subscriptions are annual and auto-renew for 12 months unless either party gives 60 days written notice before the renewal date.
- Renewal price increases are capped at 5% per year for Growth and Enterprise.
- No termination for convenience during a term. Seats can be added at any time (prorated) but reduced only at renewal.
- Payment terms: Net 30 standard. Net 45 with Finance approval. Longer terms are not offered.
- Refunds: annual fees are non-refundable except for SLA service credits. Monthly Starter customers can cancel at any time, effective at the end of the billing month.
- Customer data can be exported at any time via CSV or the API. After termination, data is retained for 90 days and then deleted within a further 30 days.

WHO TO LOOP IN
Security questionnaires: security-review team via the deal desk, 5 business day turnaround. Redlines: Legal, 7 business day turnaround. Reps must not agree to non-standard terms on a call.

TOBIAS VENKATARAMAN
Backend Engineer
Columbus, OH | tobias.venkataraman@example.com | (555) 014-2273 | github.com/tvenkat-example

SUMMARY
Backend engineer with about 6 years of experience building high-throughput services in Go and Kotlin on PostgreSQL and Kafka. Tech lead for Project Tern, the carrier-settlement rewrite at Larkspur Freight. Comfortable owning a service from design doc through launch and on-call.

EXPERIENCE

Larkspur Freight | Software Engineer II, Backend | Columbus, OH | Mar 2023 - Present
- Tech lead for Project Tern, a rewrite of the carrier-settlement service from a Rails monolith into three Go services; coordinated a working group of 4 engineers and 1 QA analyst over 7 months.
- Cut p95 latency of the rate-quote API from 820 ms to 190 ms by replacing N+1 PostgreSQL queries with a batched loader and a 90-second Redis cache keyed by lane ID.
- Designed Dockhand, a Kafka event pipeline that processes about 2.3 million shipment status events per day, using a transactional outbox table to avoid duplicate writes.
- Reduced monthly settlement mismatches from 312 to 41 with a nightly reconciliation job that compares carrier invoices against booked loads.
- Partitioned the 1.9-billion-row load_events table by month in PostgreSQL, cutting nightly vacuum time from 4 hours to 35 minutes.
- Wrote the team's first set of 14 incident runbooks; member of a 6-person on-call rotation.

Quillfeather Health | Software Engineer | Cincinnati, OH | Aug 2021 - Feb 2023
- Built the appointment-reminder service in Kotlin (Spring Boot) that sent 11 million SMS and email reminders in 2022; the no-show rate at the 9 pilot clinics fell from 18.4% to 12.9%.
- Migrated 38 cron scripts into Metronome, a single Temporal-based scheduler, removing a class of double-send bugs.
- Introduced Pact contract tests between 5 internal services, cutting integration-environment breakages from roughly 9 per month to 2.
- Implemented field-level encryption for patient phone numbers using envelope keys in AWS KMS.

Brindlecap Labs | Junior Developer | Cincinnati, OH | Aug 2020 - Jul 2021
- Maintained a Python/Django inventory tool used by 60 independent bookstores; added a CSV import that replaced a manual 3-hour weekly task.
- Wrote the product's first automated test suite, taking line coverage from 0% to 71%.
- Handled customer-support escalations one day per week.

SIDE PROJECT
Sparrowhawk (open source, maintainer since 2022)
- Go library for idempotency keys backed by PostgreSQL advisory locks; about 640 GitHub stars.
- Supports configurable key expiry and a replay-safe response cache; test suite runs against PostgreSQL 13 through 16.

EDUCATION
Ohio Valley Polytechnic University | B.S. Computer Science, Minor in Mathematics | May 2020
- Senior capstone: a route-planning simulator for municipal snowplow fleets.

SKILLS
Languages: Go, Kotlin, Python, SQL, some TypeScript
Data and messaging: PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, AWS SQS
Infrastructure: AWS (ECS, RDS, KMS), Terraform, Docker, GitHub Actions, Datadog
Practices: design docs, transactional outbox, idempotency, contract testing, on-call and runbooks

PI-A:JD.title: the job description the user is targeting
PI-A:JD.text:
SENIOR BACKEND ENGINEER, PAYMENTS & LEDGER
Tallowmarket, Inc. | Denver, CO

ABOUT TALLOWMARKET
Tallowmarket is a B2B marketplace where independent restaurants buy directly from regional farms and ranches. Our Payments & Ledger group moves about $1.1B a year through escrowed payouts to more than 6,500 growers. We are a team of 140 people, about 55 of them in engineering. Our backend is Go on PostgreSQL, with Kafka between services and Temporal for long-running payment workflows.

WHAT YOU WILL DO
- Own services in the money path: escrow holds, split payouts to growers, refunds and chargebacks.
- Design and evolve Harrow, our double-entry ledger built on PostgreSQL, as volume grows from 400,000 to a projected 1.5 million ledger entries per day.
- Improve the reliability of the nightly settlement batch that runs at 02:00 Mountain Time and must finish before banks open.
- Lead technical design reviews and mentor mid-level engineers on the team.
- Join the on-call rotation, currently one week in six.
- Partner with Finance and Risk on reconciliation and audit requirements.

WHAT YOU BRING
- 5+ years of professional backend experience in Go, Java or Kotlin.
- Deep PostgreSQL knowledge: indexing, locking, isolation levels, and safe online migrations.
- Experience with event-driven systems (Kafka, Kinesis or similar) and idempotent processing.
- A track record of leading multi-engineer projects from design doc to launch.
- Clear written communication; we make most decisions in design docs.

NICE TO HAVE
- Prior work on a double-entry ledger or a payments platform.
- Experience reducing PCI DSS scope.
- Stripe Connect or Adyen for Platforms integration experience.
- Experience with Temporal or another durable workflow engine.

WORK ARRANGEMENT
Hybrid: in our Denver LoDo office Tuesday through Thursday; Monday and Friday are flexible. Relocation assistance is available for candidates moving to the Denver metro area.

COMPENSATION
Base salary band: $172,000 - $208,000 USD, plus equity and a 6% 401(k) match. This role is leveled at L5 (Senior).

INTERVIEW PROCESS
Recruiter screen (30 minutes), a 60-minute ledger design exercise, a Go coding session, and a values conversation with our Director of Engineering, Imani Castellanos.

Tallowmarket is an equal opportunity employer.

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: To be straight with you, there's no budget for this right now. Maybe next fiscal year. And I'm not really the one who signs anyway.
items.answer: That's fair, and I'd rather know that now than build a plan around the wrong timing. Two things I'd like to understand: when your fiscal year starts, and who else weighs in on something like this. If it helps, I can put together a short summary you could pass along, so the value is clear before budget conversations start.

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: Okay so we've got about forty field techs and six people in the office doing dispatch. What would Growth actually run us for a year?
items.answer:
Growth runs **$54 per tech per month**, billed annually, so forty techs is **$25,920 a year**. Office seats are free up to five, so your sixth dispatcher adds $15 a month, about $180 a year. There's also a one-time guided implementation fee of $2,500 that covers data import, two remote training sessions and thirty days of go-live support.

So all in, you're looking at roughly **$28,600** for year one. Want me to put that in writing with the route optimization and Salesforce sync broken out?

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: Yeah so right now dispatch is basically Maria, a shared Google calendar and a lot of phone calls. It kind of works.
items.answer: That's actually a pretty common setup, and it usually holds until volume picks up. When it does, the cracks show in double bookings, missed calls, and Maria becoming the single point of failure. What does a bad week look like for you today, where does it break first?

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: They're wrapping up. Give me a clean next-steps line to end the call.
items.answer: Thanks for the time today. I'll send a short recap with what we covered and the one or two things I owe you, and I'll follow up to lock in the next conversation. What's the best day next week for a quick 30 minutes?

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: They want net 90.
items.answer: Net 90 is a big ask on our side, so let me be straight with you: our standard terms are shorter than that, and stretching to 90 days ties up a lot of working capital. That said, I'd rather find a structure that works than lose the deal over terms. What's driving the 90 days on your end, is it your own receivables cycle or a board policy?

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: Great, then just put that in writing in the order form and we can sign this week.
conversation: PROSPECT (heard): Your quick reference sheet that got forwarded to us says single sign-on comes with Growth. So we're good on Okta at the Growth price, yes?

NATIVELY: I want to get this right, because the sheet you saw is a draft and it contradicts itself. The plan page lists SSO with Okta under Growth, but the security FAQ says SAML SSO is on Enterprise. So I'm not going to confirm Okta at the Growth price off that page. Let me check with RevOps and my manager and come back to you with the correct plan and price. In the meantime, what's driving the Okta requirement for you?
items.answer: I can't put Okta at the Growth price in writing yet, because I don't have the correct plan confirmed. What I can do today is send you the order form with the plan and price left open, and hold the signature slot for this week. As soon as RevOps and my manager confirm which plan carries Okta, I'll fill it in and send it straight back to you. While I chase that, what's driving the Okta requirement on your side?

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: Does it work offline?
items.answer: It does, with some limits. The core features work without a connection, and anything that needs syncing catches up once I'm back online. What would you need it to do offline?

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: Okay, our IT guy sent me a list. Do you do SSO with Okta on the Growth plan, where exactly is our data stored, are you ISO 27001 certified, and will you sign a BAA? We do service calls at a few medical clinics.
items.answer: Straight answers: SSO with Okta is Enterprise only, so Growth uses email and password with optional authenticator-app 2FA. Data sits in AWS US Ohio by default, with EU residency in Frankfurt on Enterprise. We're not ISO 27001 certified, and we don't sign BAAs, since the product isn't built to store protected health information. If those are hard requirements, Enterprise plus a security review is the path. Want me to get our security team on a call with your IT guy?

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: They're also talking to Routewise. Give me one question I can ask that gets them thinking about switching costs, no trash talk.
items.answer: They're weighing two options, so the useful question is about what it costs them to move, not what Routewise does wrong. Something like: "If you did switch, what would have to be rebuilt or retrained on your side, and who'd carry that work?" That gets them naming the real switching cost themselves, and it tells you where you can take weight off their plate. Want me to follow it with a question about their timeline for deciding?

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: They just asked why they should trust me to run their rollout. Tell them a bit about my background.
items.answer: I'd rather earn that than assert it. What I bring is a clear plan, a named owner for each step, and checkpoints where you see progress before we go further. Tell me what a rollout has to get right on your side, and I'll show you how I'd run it.
